Lefana or rice fan. Flat, circular tray woven in check weave using black and natural cane strips to create a zigzag pattern; rim is reinforced with lengths of cane and wrapped in cane strips; small loop attached to one side. Used for winnowing.
Large, undecorated spoon with flat bowl and straight handle. Splash marls present on surface.
Curved rectangular stool on four rectangular legs, one cracked. Decorated with lightly incised geometric designs on seat.
Carved wooden spoon with loop as handle. Burnt decoration present on both sides, featuring small black circles.

Carved wooden stool with a head at one end, and a curved tail at other. Seat is curved inward; the two legs are carved into a 'v' shape. Surface features incised linear and geometric decoration. Carved from a single piece of wood.
Bamena; Musaia. Cylindrical wooden snuff box with one tapering end decorated with grooved lines. The lid is a disc, probably of gourd, with a tassel of cotton fibres extending from the centre.
Metal key, tied to a long piece of wood with a section carved out of centre and line decoration on rear. The adhered Thomas label notes "lock and key".

Kondoinye. Powder measure made from a spherical gourd which has been hollowed and cut at one side to create a circular opening.  The surface of the gourd is very dark and has many hairline cracks in it. There is a leather loop attached to the base of the measure and there are signs of historic insect presence.
Circular stool set with central leg, with rectangular base. Pecked and incised line decoration on seat and leg.
Lefa. Flat, circular calabash cover made of coiled plant fibre. Fibre is in neutral tones and black creating rings and alternating patterns.
A stool carved from one piece of wood with circular seat and four tapered legs.
Whip made of woven fibre.
Carved oblong box.
Iron adze head with slightly curved blade and triangular tang.

Sabsdi. Iron key with a hollow shaft, circular cross-section, decorated with four parallel horizontal lines. Loop at one end and at the other end, a rectangular protrusion 'bit' with two cut-out notches at. Attached to the loop is a loop of plaited leather.
Metal key tied to a long piece of wood, with a section carved out of centre and line decoration on rear. The adhered Thomas label notes "lock and key".
Sabsdi. Iron key. Circular cross-section shaft with a loop at one end and at the other end, two rectangular protrusions 'bit'. Attached to the loop is a loop of plaited leather.

Sabsdi. Iron key. Shaft with circular cross-section, decorated with two sets of three parallel horizontal lines. Loop at one end and at the other end, a rectangular protrusion 'bit' with one large cut-out notch. Attached to the loop is a loop of plaited leather.

Sabsdi. Brass key. Shaft with oval cross-section, decorated in two places with incised horizontal lines, very worn. Loop at one end of the shaft, rectangular protrusion 'bit' with two cut-out notches at the other end. Attached to the loop is a loop of plaited leather.

Lefana or rice fan. Flat, circular tray woven in check weave using black and natural cane strips to create a zigzag pattern; rim is reinforced with lengths of cane and wrapped in cane strips; small loop attached to one side. Used for winnowing.

textile.title: Ceramic spindle attached to wooden whorl.
Wooden loom pulley with a loop of rope attached to top.
Composite textile. Two strips of woven textile alternating with three bands of crochet; central band of crochet has a diamond pattern.
Wooden loom pulley with plant fibre tied through top.

jewelry.title: Koinasehe. Short necklace with three hemispherical and two rectangular charms separated by small beads of red braided leather. The hemispherical charms are made from black leather, decoratively sewn at the edge with a light coloured plant fibre, while the rectangular charms are made from red leather sewn at the edges with dark thread. These charms are attached to a length of black braided leather cord with red leather knots at the end for securing around the neck. The contents of the charms are unknown.
Tagalena. A necklace consisting of four long strands of red seeds or beans strung on fibre. The seeds are drilled lengthways to allow them to be strung.
Kolona. Hair ornament made from a section of a shell. The white shell has been cut horizontally and the spiral formation is clearly visible.
Sabsdi; Afua ika. Short necklace of black seeds, a hole drilled in them to allow them to be strung as a necklace.
Sabsdi. Two necklets of black seed beads on fibre. The fibre has broken and many of the beads are loose.

arms.title: Simple bow made from cane (.1). Length of cane with a notch at either end and the remains of a cane strip string; cylindrical section of cane with a hole drilled through one end and a length of cotton attaching it to the bow, possibly part of an arrow (.2).

instruments.title: Tamba. Double head hourglass drum [.1], made of dark brown wood, with a band of incised line decoration around the waist. The two leather skins are laced in place with fibre strings that run the full length of the drum. There is a ring of twisted rope just below the edge of both skins. The beater [.2] consists of a stick of palm rib, with a shorter piece sticking out at a right angle.

A guitar made from wood, leather, hair and iron. The body is formed from a hollowed piece of wood, with piece of leather stretched across the opening and held taught with little wooden pegs. The neck is formed from a straight piece of wood and sits below the leather, with a bridge of wood attached and exiting from a hole cut into the leather.  The neck has four ties of leather strips which originally held the strings of plaited hair in place. Broken sections of string remain attached and there is a small iron wire loop at the side of the body.
Two identical flutes made from straight, hollow pieces of reed, with three tone holes burnt into one end and a single embouchure hole burnt into the other. Both flutes have split in places.

architectural.title: Small, decorated wooden door. The door is made from a rectangular piece of wood with wooden strips (two with serrated edges) attached with metal staples near the edges to form a frame.  The surface is carved with geometric designs and painted with black and red pigments.

masks-ritual.title: Kulla. A flywhisk made from a cow tail. One half wrapped in cloth, with a loop of string attached at one end, and light coloured hair attached by string at the other end.

Necklet of five rectangular leather charms strung on a long braided leather cord. The contents of the charms are unknown, but they are all of similar dimensions and are covered in leather sewn with dark thread. The central charm has a triangular raised area of decoration. The charms are separated by small braided leather knots and the long cord has a sliding knot fastening system.
